Article 56-2 — Event Data Recorder

① The term “accidents such as vehicle collisions as determined by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport” in Article 2(10) of the Motor Vehicle Management Act refers to situations where any of the following occurs: [Amended 2024-11-29, 2025-02-14]

The cumulative change in speed in the direction of travel reaches 8 km/h or more within 0.15 seconds (for vehicles that record lateral speed changes, this also includes cases where the cumulative lateral speed change reaches 8 km/h or more within 0.15 seconds).

An irreversible safety device such as an airbag or seat belt pre-tensioner deploys.

A safety device installed outside the passenger compartment to mitigate injury to pedestrians and others in a collision with a pedestrian or cyclist (hereinafter “pedestrian protection system”) deploys.

② The term “vehicles meeting criteria determined by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, such as vehicle type, purpose, and passenger capacity” in Article 29-3(1) of the Motor Vehicle Management Act refers to the following vehicles: [Amended 2025-02-14]

Passenger cars (excluding ultra-compact passenger cars)

0.1.2 This Standard may also be cited as ADR 28/01.

0.2 COMMENCEMENT

0.2.1 This Standard commences on the day after it is registered.

0.3.1 This Standard repeals each vehicle standard with the name ADR 28/01, and each amendment of such a standard, that is:

(a) made under section 7 of the Motor Vehicles Standard Act 1989; and

§ 571.217a Standard No. 217a; Anti-ejection glazing for bus portals; Mandatory applicability beginning October 30, 2027.

S1. Scope. This standard establishes requirements to improve side and roof bus portals by way of glazing that is highly resistant to partial or complete occupant ejection in all types of crashes.

S2. Purpose. The purpose of this standard is to reduce death and injuries resulting from complete and partial ejections of bus occupants through side and roof portals during rollovers and other crashes.

S3. Application.

(a) Subject to S3(b) of this section, this standard applies to:

(1) Over-the-road buses manufactured on or after October 30, 2027, and

(2) Buses, other than over-the-road buses, that have a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) greater than 11,793 kilograms (kg) manufactured on or after October 30, 2027.

(b) This standard does not apply to school buses, transit buses, prison buses, and perimeter-seating buses.

§ 571.119 Standard No. 119; New pneumatic tires for motor vehicles with a GVWR of more than 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds), specialty tires, and tires for motorcycles.

S1. Scope. This standard establishes performance and marking requirements for tires for use on motor vehicles with a GVWR of more than 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds), specialty tires, and tires for motorcycles.

S2. Purpose. The purpose of this standard is to provide safe operational performance levels for tires used on motor vehicles with a GVWR of more than 10,000 pounds, trailers, and motorcycles, and to place sufficient information on the tires to permit their proper selection and use.

S3. Application. This standard applies to:

(a) New pneumatic tires for use on motor vehicles with a GVWR of more than 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds) manufactured after 1948;

(b) New pneumatic light truck tires with a tread depth of 18/32 inch or greater, for use on motor vehicles with a GVWR of 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds) or less manufactured after 1948;

(c) Tires for use on special-use trailers (ST, FI and 8-12 rim or lower diameter code); and

(d) Tires for use on motorcycles manufactured after 1948.

S4. Definitions.

Curated reference, not legal advice. Confirm the current instrument, series and transitional dates with the authority before any certification decision.

AUTHORITIES
NHTSA ↗ — Vehicle safety (FMVSS), recalls, CAFE, theft, EDR
US EPA ↗ — Exhaust/evap emissions, fuel-economy test procedures & labels, refrigerants (SNAP)
California Air Resources Board (CARB) ↗ — California + Section 177 states emissions/ZEV (LEV IV, ACC II)
FCC ↗ — Intentional radiators (keyless entry, radar, telematics) — 47 CFR Part 15/95
APPROVAL PROCESS
Register as a manufacturer: Part 565 requires manufacturer-identifier information at least 60 days before affixing the first VIN using it; VIN-decoding information is due at least 60 days before offering the first vehicle for sale, or within one week after unavailable vehicle-characteristic information first becomes available. Part 566 manufacturer identification is due within 30 days of beginning manufacture.
Foreign manufacturers designate a US agent for service of process (49 CFR 551 Subpart D).
Self-certify to every applicable FMVSS — no government pre-approval; keep a test/engineering file because NHTSA's OVSC runs post-sale compliance tests.
Obtain EPA (and CARB Executive Order where sold in CA/§177 states) Certificate of Conformity BEFORE introduction into commerce.
Import: CBP entry with HS-7 declaration (box 2A for conforming vehicles) and EPA Form 3520-1.
Post-market: defect & noncompliance reports within 5 working days (Part 573), owner notification (Part 577), quarterly Early Warning Reporting (Part 579).
MARKS, LABELS & CERTIFICATES
Certification label on door pillar (49 CFR 567) — manufacturer certifies compliance with all applicable FMVSS, bumper (Part 581) and theft (Part 541) standards
Tire & loading information placard (FMVSS 110)
EPA Certificate of Conformity + Vehicle Emission Control Information (VECI) label (40 CFR 86/1066)
Monroney window sticker (15 U.S.C. 1232) with EPA/NHTSA fuel economy & environment label (40 CFR 600 Subpart D)
Parts marking for high-theft lines (49 CFR 541) unless exempted under Part 543
ACCEPTED FOREIGN APPROVALS / EVIDENCE
None — national certification required
EMISSIONS & ENERGY

EPA Tier 3 → 2027+ criteria-pollutant standards. EPA rescinded the GHG endangerment finding and ALL federal vehicle GHG standards (final rule published 18 Feb 2026). CARB LEV III applies in California; the federal waiver for Advanced Clean Cars II (LEV IV / ZEV) was revoked by Congress under the CRA (12 Jun 2025) and is in litigation. Fuel economy: NHTSA CAFE reset for MY2022–2031 (SAFE Vehicles Rule III, FR 30 Sep 2026, effective 30 Nov 2026; credit trading eliminated).

LANGUAGE

English (Spanish additionally expected for Puerto Rico consumer information)

WATCH LIST — UPCOMING CHANGES
FMVSS 127 — AEB incl. pedestrian AEB for light vehicles (final rule 2024; compliance phase-in from Sept 2029; subject to reconsideration petitions).
FMVSS 305a — EV electrical safety incl. REESS (final rule 2024).
Rear-seat belt reminder (FMVSS 208 amendment) and proposed heavy-vehicle AEB.
Connected-vehicle import/sale prohibition for VCS/ADS hardware & software tied to China/Russia (15 CFR 791, BIS, final rule Jan 2025; software MY2027, hardware MY2030).
NOTES
States cannot set different safety standards (federal preemption), but CARB and §177 states set emissions; Massachusetts has a telematics right-to-repair law.
Low-volume / small manufacturers: Part 555 temporary exemptions; replica vehicle program (Part 586).
Gray-market imports must be brought into compliance by a Registered Importer (Part 592) and are only possible for vehicles NHTSA has determined eligible (Part 593).
